name: OpenStack Glance - Image Service
description:
The Glance project provides a service where users can upload and discover data assets that are meant to be used with other services. This currently includes images and metadata definitions.

The OpenStack Image Service acts as a registry for virtual disk images. Users can add new images or take a snapshot of an image from an existing server for immediate storage. Use snapshots for back up and as templates to launch new servers.

name: Install DevStack
description:
This page is exactly same as previously discussed feel free to just copy/paste the commands,once dashboard is login and move to next step. If you want to re-read ..go on.. We will recap our installation with DevStack.DevStack is a set of scripts which will install all the OpenStack components and prepare them ready for your use.

We need to run below steps to install devstack setup. we covered these steps on OpenStack basics under topic Install and Configure DevStack. You can copy/paste them into right side terminal.

sudo apt-get update 
sudo apt-get -y git
Lets add a new user 
sudo adduser --disabled-password --gecos "" stack 
sudo su <<EOF
echo "stack ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD: ALL" >> /etc/sudoers
EOF
Now lets setup devstack repo and launch the installation script. 
sudo su stack <<EOF
cd /home/stack 
git clone https://git.openstack.org/openstack-dev/devstack  -b stable/kilo openstack
cd /home/stack/openstack/
echo '[[local|localrc]]' >  /home/stack/openstack/local.conf
echo ADMIN_PASSWORD=password >>  /home/stack/openstack/local.conf
echo MYSQL_PASSWORD=password >>  /home/stack/openstack/local.conf
echo RABBIT_PASSWORD=password >>  /home/stack/openstack/local.conf
echo SERVICE_PASSWORD=password >>  /home/stack/openstack/local.conf
echo SERVICE_TOKEN=tokentoken >>  /home/stack/openstack/local.conf

echo CINDER_BRANCH=stable/kilo >> /home/stack/openstack/local.conf
echo GLANCE_BRANCH=stable/kilo >> /home/stack/openstack/local.conf
echo HORIZON_BRANCH=stable/kilo >> /home/stack/openstack/local.conf
echo KEYSTONE_BRANCH=stable/kilo >> /home/stack/openstack/local.conf
echo NEUTRON_BRANCH=stable/kilo >> /home/stack/openstack/local.conf
echo NOVA_BRANCH=stable/kilo >> /home/stack/openstack/local.conf
EOF

Just one more thing to add on config file before running the script. We need to set HOST_IP. You can fetch it from /root/ directory. Just do
sudo ls /root
52.11.130.199 tmp
the ip-address will be different for you, so update properly and execute the script as user 'stack'. 
echo HOST_IP=52.11.130.199 >> /home/stack/openstack/local.conf
sudo su stack 
#move to stack home dir and execute script as
cd ~  
/home/stack/openstack/stack.sh
This installation will take around 20 to 30 minutes, Please feel free leave this machine and take a break :)

name: Access Dashboard
description:
Now you need to access OpenStack Dashboard, horizon. So point your browser to your HOST_IP ipaddress 
 http://HOST_IP
You will see the OpenStack Dashboard Login page, use admin/password to complete login process.

name: Launch an Instance
description:
Today, we will learn about Image Service code named Glance.
After logging into the dashboard, Launch an "Cirros" instance from .."Oh stop,stop" we can hear you screaming :)

Even we are little bored using same image again and again. Whyn't we launch a Ubuntu instance!. In order to launch a Ubuntu Instance, we need a Ubuntu Image.

Thankfully, OpenStack has Cloud images we will use the most recent version of the 64-bit QCOW2 image for Ubuntu 14.04 named trusty-server-cloudimg-amd64-disk1.img.

name: Create an Image
description:
On the Dashboard follow Compute->Image->Create Image We will set only important fields here. Set 
 
Name as Ubuntu 
Image Source as Image location  
Image location as http://uec-images.ubuntu.com/trusty/current/trusty-server-cloudimg-amd64-disk1.img
Format as QCOW2-QEMU Emulator
Final click Create to download the image into our Glance.

name: Launch using new Image
description:
We didn't hear any screams this time :-) So we will do Compute->Launch Instances set following details 
Availability Zone : nova
Name : ubuntu 
Flavor : m1.nano
Instance Count : 1
Instance Boot Source : Boot from image
Boot Image : Ubuntu
So far we filled the Details tab now Click on Post-Creation tab. We need to set password for this Cloud-Ubuntu image with customized script. Select Direct Input and just paste below content into it 
#cloud-config
password: password
chpasswd: { expire: False }
ssh_pwauth: True
Wait for instance state to become running, Click on Instance name which is Ubuntu. Now you will see 4 tabs like Overview Log Console Action Log Click on Console and please login using username/password "ubuntu/password"

We are logged into an instance with the help of newly added Glance Ubuntu image. That's pretty simple too, right? - Just play around with Glance to get more familiar. See you in next session.
